thread.title: Apple Seen Sticking With Finisar, Which May Get An Overhaul

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Apple Seen Sticking With Finisar, Which May Get An Overhaul
text:
Finisar ( FNSR ) remains an optical device supplier to Apple ( AAPL ) despite speculation over the iPhone maker's supply chain, says one analyst who also sees Finisar restructuring to help bring life back to its stock.
X Shares in Finisar, a maker of optical components, popped on Thursday but are down 19% in 2018 and 33% from a year ago. Shares rallied in December after Apple announced it would finance Finisar's ramp-up of a 3D sensor manufacturing plant in Texas.
But Finisar stock has weakened since rival Lumentum Holding ( LITE ) announced its acquisition of Oclaro ( OCLR ), a deal analysts said could be a precursor to industry consolidation. Finisar stock has also weakened on speculation that II-VI ( IIVI ), another maker of 3D sensors, could win more business from Apple.
Both Lumentum and Finisar provide Apple with 3D sensors, also called vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs), used in facial recognition, analysts say.

Please contact customer service CLOSE More Pain To Lumentum "If it is indeed true that II-VI is gearing up capacity to supply VCSELs to Apple, it should cause more pain to Lumentum than Finisar, given the unit volumes that each of these vendors ship today and/or will be shipping to Apple for the remainder of the year," Dmitry Netis, a William Blair analyst, said in a note to clients. "We believe that II-VI may be ramping up the low-powered VCSELs, which Finisar does not manufacture. Finisar, at Apple's request, has been focused on high-powered VCSELs out of its 4-inch Allen, Texas, fab."
Finisar stock popped 6.3% to close at 15.62 on the stock market today . Lumentum rose 2.9% to 60.50. II-VI gained 1.5% to 42.10.
Netis says Finisar stock is now trading at book value, giving investors a chance to pounce ahead of a possible merger, leveraged buyout, or company reorganization. That restructuring could come at its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call in June.
"We view as highly likely an organic restructuring plan by the new CEO, expected to be revealed on the earnings call in early June," Netis said.
